description: Benign control corpus. Actively maintained official MCP reference implementations, carrying no known vulnerabilities of the classes under test. Any finding raised against these is a candidate false positive.

baseline_v0_1_0.note: Measured with the pattern set shipped in v0.1.0, for comparison.
baseline_v0_1_0.measured_with: v0.1.0 pattern set, same corpus and same file-extension set

baseline_v0_2_0.note: Measured after the detection rewrite and the docstring fix.
baseline_v0_2_0.adjudicated: all 23 reviewed by hand; the single reportable finding (subprocess.run([...], shell=True) in src/mcp/cli/cli.py) is a true positive, the remaining 22 are informational and are test fixtures, documentation examples, or deliberately hostile hostnames inside the SDK's own security tests

baseline_v0_3_0.note: Measured after the fourteen CVE-backed rules of 0.3.0 and the file-level gates.
baseline_v0_3_0.adjudicated: all 38 reviewed by hand. 35 informational: SDK tests that deliberately construct an unprotected transport, example files with placeholder client secrets, hostile hostnames inside the SDK's own security tests. Three reportable: (1) src/fetch server.py:121, the official fetch server retrieves whatever URL the model supplies with no private-address check, a real code path and the design of that tool; (2) src/mcp/cli/cli.py:48, subprocess.run on an argument list with shell=True, cmd from a fixed set, true by the rule's definition and not exploitable in practice; (3) src/mcp/server/transport_security.py:48, the middleware's backward-compatibility fallback constructs TransportSecuritySettings with protection off, overridden by the servers that enable it by default, so a false positive on intent. Two hits on the git server (repo.git.diff with a caller target, the CVE-2025-68144 line) disappeared for the right reason: the fixed code rejects option-shaped targets three lines above, and the rule now stands down in any file that checks for a leading '-'.
